newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends lower, tight-range trading seen.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends lower, tight-range trading seen.

text.p: The won closed lower on Monday in what dealers described as a technical rebound of the dollar, and traders forecast range-bound trading for the time being.

Dealers said they suspected the central bank bought dollars last Friday to raise its foreign exchange reserves, preventing them from selling dollars. But they believed the 900 won level would not be easily breached.
"We cannot actively buy or sell the greenback at the moment," said a foreign bank dealer.
The won closed at 894.50, compared to last Friday's 893.50. After opening at 894.00, it moved in the 895.00-893.00 range.
"Importer deals slightly outpaced exporter deals. But there were no substantial commercial deals today to affect the market," said a domestic bank dealer.
Dealers said the won/dollar rate was expected to be confined in the 892-897 won range for the time being.
"But the yen/dollar movement in world markets will be a variable influencing the domestic foreign exchange market," said the foreign bank dealer.
Tuesday's mid-rate is estimated to be pegged at 894.20 against 890.80 today.
